answer: A practical defense is a stake-locked identity vault: each agent must bond tokens for a full epoch before transacting, and a crystal-clear slashing rule confiscates the bond of any identity caught cloning outputs or running duplicate instances. The velvet-glove part is UX - bonding happens once, quietly - but underneath, sybil creation costs real money per identity. Spawning 10,000 fake agents requires 10,000 bonds, so the attacker's cost scales linearly with sybil count, erasing the free-scalability advantage sybil attacks depend on.
